fixes.explanation: Holy it is, baker! The LORD says, “Consecrate yourselves, therefore, and be holy, because I am the LORD your God.” (Leviticus 20:7) All those heavy warnings come before it, and then He says what He wants for His people. I think it lands like a hand on the shoulder after a hard talk. And the reason He gives is who He is, not a list of rules.

Wise is a good one, friend, and I wish I'd had more of it when I picked my hiding spots. But the LORD says, “Consecrate yourselves, therefore, and be holy…” (Leviticus 20:7) The word He picks is holy. Set apart for Him is the whole call here, and it's the answer on this card.

This one is true, friend, and I get why False looked tempting after all those serious warnings. But look at the very next verse. The LORD says, “And you shall keep My statutes and practice them.” (Leviticus 20:8) Keeping them and practicing them both sit in that one sentence, and He adds, “I am the LORD who sanctifies you.” So it isn't only a list of don'ts.

I know, friend. After a sermon this heavy, a promise can feel too good to be true. But it's right there: “But I have told you that you will inherit their land, since I will give it to you as an inheritance…” (Leviticus 20:24) The LORD says it plainly, and He says it ahead of time. So this one is True, and the land is a gift, not something they earn.

Box-worthy pick, baker! The LORD calls it “…a land flowing with milk and honey.” (Leviticus 20:24) Picture that for a second. It's so full of good things that it's overflowing, like dough rising right over the edge of the bowl. And He says He will give it to them as an inheritance.
